newsitem.title: USA: JonBenet's parents have right to view testing.
newsitem.headline: JonBenet's parents have right to view testing.

text.p: Lawyers for the parents of slain beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey will be allowed to view how tests are being conducted on key scientific evidence in the case, a spokesman said on Thursday.

"Legal counsel for the Ramsey family are being provided an opportunity to observe the Cellmark (DNA) testing," Kelvin McNeill said. He added that prosecutors believe the family may have appropriate "standing" to be present and that officials have decided to follow a conservative course on the matter.

The child's body was found Dec. 26 by her father, John Ramsey, in a windowless basement of the family's home in Boulder, Colorado, some eight hours after her mother, Patricia, said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000. No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the 12-week probe.

Legal sources said Boulder police were being especially cautious in allowing a family representative to view the testing. The DNA evidence was sent to Cellmark Laboratories in Maryland on March 4 and testing typically takes four to six weeks.
"We are comfortable with the pace of the investigation. It is on track and moving forward," McNeill told reporters, adding that police have held 176 formal interviews.

He said additional samples of "non-testimonial evidence" such as hair or handwriting samples were being gathered as police speak with others who may have had access to the crime scene. He also said Boulder police met twice last week with private investigators hired by the Ramsey family but he declined to disclose any details.
No formal face-to-face police interview of the parents has been scheduled, McNeill said.
The Colorado Bureau of Investigation continues to analyse handwriting samples, including those of Patricia Ramsey, he said.
